title: The sacrifices of touring and being the wrong colour
summary: Hodes talks about poor rooms in Europe and being told he is the wrong colour for the blues in France.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, this is what I mean. There are sacrifices and you should get paid for it, if you're going to do this. And so some places you win, and some places you fail. Then you run into this other thing. You're the wrong color. Somebody says, you can't come to France to play blues because you're the wrong color. And I see some -- if I use the word bum, I mean musical bum, who's the right color but he can't play blues. He's hardly playing, and he's getting over quite often. And you wonder. That's the other side of it.

It's all part of the picture. You don't get bitter about it. It's just one of those things. People -- and the final analysis, what you're up against is ignorance. I mean, if you didn't have ignorance --
